passage:
'Leela, Mama's just going to get the clothes off the line.'
'Mama! Mama!'
'Two minutes, sweetheart. Papa's right here.'
'Noooo! Mama!'
'Look, Leela, blocks!'
Papa calls through the balcony door, 'Ayesha, she's standing at the door, crying.'
'Coming!' Ayesha hurries in, and two-year-old Leela runs to her Mama and hiccups into her kurta.
'See? Back already.'
Later the three of them eat quietly, Leela's hand on Mama's sleeve.

qa.q: What was Mama going to do when she left the room?
qa.a: She was going to get the clothes off the line.

qa.q: What was Leela feeling when Mama went to the balcony, and what shows it?
qa.a: Leela felt upset and afraid that Mama was gone; she kept calling 'Mama!', refused the blocks and stood crying at the door.

qa.q: What could the parents try so short separations feel easier for Leela?
qa.a: Say a warm goodbye, tell her when Mama will be back, and sometimes let her come along or watch, so she learns Mama always returns.

qa.q: What is it like for Papa when Leela refuses his blocks and cries for Mama?
qa.a: Papa may feel a bit helpless or left out, because his comfort is not enough in that moment even though he is right there.

grounding: Shows a toddler in a small family who is closely bonded to one caregiver and becomes sharply distressed when that caregiver leaves the room.

passage:
Playgroup note, Tuesday. Tanuja, room teacher.
Aadhya, two, lives with just her parents; her days are usually quiet. When her father waved and left, she cried hard and held the door handle a long time, deaf to the other children. I sat near her without pulling her away and said, 'You miss Papa.' She let me read her the duck book. At pickup she ran to him and would not let go. I have asked him to stay five minutes tomorrow.

qa.q: What book did Tanuja read to Aadhya later?
qa.a: The duck book.

qa.q: How was Aadhya feeling when her father left, and what shows it?
qa.a: She felt very upset and lost without Papa; she cried hard and held the door handle for a long time, not noticing the other children.

qa.q: Which of Tanuja's steps helped, and what else could help tomorrow?
qa.a: Sitting close and naming the feeling helped; tomorrow, Papa staying a few minutes before a clear, cheerful goodbye may help Aadhya settle.

qa.q: How might Aadhya's father feel when she runs to him and will not let go at pickup?
qa.a: He may feel loved and also a little worried, seeing how strongly she depends on him and her mother.

grounding: Illustrates a toddler from a small family whose deep bond with one or two caregivers shows as sharp distress when one of them leaves.

passage:
Tuesday: Papa Zubin shut the bathroom door for one minute. Kavitha, two, hammered on it and screamed until he opened it.

Thursday: When Mama left for her night shift, Kavitha clung to the door handle and sobbed for a long time, then fell asleep on Papa's chest.

Sunday: No visitors, no noise. Just Kavitha, Papa and Mama on the floor, building block towers all afternoon. Kavitha patted Papa's cheek every time a tower fell.

qa.q: What did Kavitha do when Papa shut the bathroom door?
qa.a: Kavitha hammered on it and screamed until he opened it.

qa.q: What was Kavitha feeling when Mama left for her night shift?
qa.a: Kavitha was deeply upset and scared to see her go, clinging to the door handle and sobbing until she fell asleep on Papa's chest.

qa.q: How could Papa and Mama ease their exits for Kavitha?
qa.a: Give a short, cheerful goodbye every time and leave her busy with the other parent, so leaving becomes predictable.

qa.q: What is it like for Papa Zubin when Kavitha screams at the bathroom door?
qa.a: He may feel touched to be needed so much and also worn out by never getting a minute alone.

grounding: Shows a toddler in a small nuclear home deeply tied to two parents, with sharp distress at brief separations and quiet shared days.

passage: In their two-room flat in Pune, Disha, eighteen months old, banged a steel bowl while her father, Chinmay, answered emails. When he stepped onto the balcony to hang the washing, she dropped the bowl and screamed, arms stretched to the glass door. The neighbour aunty who dropped by with laddoos tried to pick her up; Disha arched away, sobbing. Only when Chinmay came back did she go limp on his shoulder.

qa.q: What did the neighbour aunty bring?
qa.a: The neighbour aunty dropped by with laddoos.

qa.q: Why did Disha arch away from the neighbour aunty?
qa.a: Disha was frightened and wanted only her father; a less familiar face could not comfort her the way Chinmay could.

qa.q: What could Chinmay try before stepping out to the balcony?
qa.a: Tell Disha where he is going, keep her where she can see him, and come back quickly; small predictable steps can ease her panic.

qa.q: How might the neighbour aunty feel when Disha pulls away?
qa.a: The neighbour aunty might feel a bit awkward or rejected, though she may understand that Disha knows only a few faces well.

grounding: Shows a toddler in a nuclear home tied closely to one caregiver, with sharp distress when he leaves the room and no comfort from a less familiar adult.

passage:
"Let me try, na," said Granny, lifting Himani from the cot. "I put four children to sleep in my time."
Himani stiffened. "Mama! Mama!"
"She's just tired," said Francis from the doorway.
"Come, sweetheart, Granny will sing."
Himani twisted, reaching past her shoulder toward the kitchen.
Mum hurried in, wiping her hands. "I'm here, baby."
Himani flung herself across and went silent in Mum's neck.
Granny laughed a little sadly. "Only two faces for this one, hmm?"
"She'll warm up by the end of your visit, Ma," Francis said.

qa.q: How many children did Granny say she had put to sleep?
qa.a: Granny said she put four children to sleep in her time.

qa.q: What does Himani's twisting toward the kitchen suggest?
qa.a: Himani felt upset and unsafe with Granny and wanted Mum, one of her two main faces, to comfort her.

qa.q: What could help Himani warm up to Granny during the visit?
qa.a: Let Granny join daytime play with Mum close by first, so she becomes familiar before trying bedtime alone.

qa.q: What is it like for Granny when Himani calms only for Mum?
qa.a: Granny feels a little sad and left out, though she laughs it off and accepts Himani has only two faces for now.

grounding: Shows a toddler in a nuclear home who accepts comfort only from her parents, with deep but narrow bonds.

passage:
Creche note, Tuesday.
At drop-off Kunal clung to his mother Dolma's neck. When she left, he screamed and stood at the door, palms flat on the glass. Other adults' arms did not help. He took my hand only after twenty minutes, still sniffing. When Dolma came back, he ran and buried his face. I suggested she stay five minutes tomorrow and wave clearly before leaving.

qa.q: Where did Kunal stand after his mother left?
qa.a: He stood at the door, palms flat on the glass.

qa.q: What was Kunal feeling when Dolma left the creche?
qa.a: He was very distressed and frightened, screaming and pressing against the glass.

qa.q: What did the carer suggest for tomorrow, and why might it help?
qa.a: That Dolma stay five minutes and wave clearly, so Kunal can settle and know she is going and will come back.

qa.q: How might Dolma feel at drop-off?
qa.a: She probably feels torn and sad leaving him crying, and relieved when he runs to her.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler closely tied to one parent who shows sharp distress when she leaves.
